stem: Which section of the ZIMSEC project report is worth 15 marks?

options.content: Section A: selection, investigation and analysis

explanation: Section D is worth 15 marks.

stem: Where should completed questionnaires and interview answers be placed in the report?

options.rationale: Correct: they are evidence of the research.
The cover page carries the title and details.
The contents page lists sections and pages.

explanation: Bulky evidence goes in the appendices.

stem: A program accepts ages from 12 to 18. Which value is extreme (boundary) test data?

options.rationale: 11 is abnormal data, just outside the range.
Correct: it is valid and on the lower limit.

explanation: Extreme data is valid data at the limits of the range.

stem: Which document explains to the client how to install, start and use the system?

options.rationale: This checks whether the solution is worthwhile.

explanation: User documentation is written for the client.

stem: According to the project guide, what is the limit on the length of the project?

options.content: 50 pages including all of the appendices

explanation: The limit is 50 pages excluding appendices.

stem: What does a feasibility study check?

options.content: Whether the program has any spelling mistakes
Whether the proposed solution is possible and worthwhile
Whether the report is spiral bound
Which colour to use on the cover page
options.rationale: That is not a feasibility question.

explanation: A feasibility study checks technical, economic and operational factors.
hints: Is it done at the start or the end of the project?

stem: Which objective is best written for a project, so that it can be tested?

options.content: The bursar can find a learner's balance in under ten seconds
The users will like the system very much when it is finished

explanation: Objectives should be specific and measurable.
hints: Can you test it and get a yes or no?

stem: Which statement would earn most credit in the evaluation of a project?

options.content: The system works perfectly and has no faults, the user was extremely happy with every part of it, and nothing needs to be improved
options.rationale: No system is perfect and the claim has no evidence.

options.content: The system was finished on time
options.rationale: This says nothing about the objectives.
This has no evidence or detail.

options.content: Objectives 1 to 4 were met, shown by the tests; objective 5 was not met because reports cannot be printed, and printing is planned as an improvement
options.rationale: Correct: it is honest, linked to the objectives and looks forward.

explanation: An evaluation compares the result with each objective.
hints: Which answer is specific and honest?

stem: In a test plan the expected results should be written before the tests are run.
explanation: True. Expected results are decided from the requirements, so that the real result can be judged against them.

stem: Match each section of the project report to what it contains.

right.content: Well-structured code, technical documentation and user documentation
Test data, system testing and the evaluation
Depth, originality, conduct and the quality of the report
Investigation of the current system, feasibility study and requirements
Alternative methods, input, output and file design, and the test strategy

explanation: Each section has a clear purpose.

stem: Complete the sentences about test data.

payload.template: Typical valid data is {{blank:a}} data. Valid data at the limits of the range is {{blank:b}} data. Invalid data that the program must reject is {{blank:c}} data.

explanation: Standard, extreme and abnormal.

stem: Name the research tool in which a researcher asks a person questions face to face and writes down the answers.
explanation: An interview.

stem: A learner's project is marked: Section A 21, Section B 19, Section C 22, Section D 12 and Section E 7. Calculate the total mark out of 100.
explanation: 81 out of 100.

stem: A report has 38 pages of main text and 14 pages of appendices. By how many pages is the main text below the limit of 50 pages (the appendices are not counted)?
workedSolution:
1. Limit = 50 pages of main text.
2. 50 − 38 = 12 pages.
hints: Only the main text counts towards the limit of 50 pages.

stem: The project (Paper 4) carries 20% of the final grade. A learner scores 81 out of 100 for it. How many percentage points does it add to the final grade? Give your answer to one decimal place.
hints: Project marks out of 100 are worth 20% of the final grade.

stem: Describe two research tools that a learner could use to investigate the current system of a school office. [4]

points.description: Interview: ask the bursar or clerk questions face to face about how the work is done
It gives detailed answers and explanations of problems
Questionnaire or record inspection: many staff answer the same questions, or the learner reads the existing paper records
It gives comparable answers from many people, or shows the real data and forms in use

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An interview with the bursar gives detailed answers about how the work is done and what problems there are. A questionnaire given to many staff gives comparable answers, and inspecting the paper records shows the real forms and data in use.

explanation: Two tools and their value.
hints: Two tools with a use for each.

stem: State what the user documentation of a project should contain. [4]

points.description: How to install the system
How to start the system
How to use it (navigation), with screens and examples
How to exit the system, what the error messages mean and what to do if something goes wrong

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: How to install the system, how to start it, how to use and navigate it with screens and examples, and how to exit it, including what the messages mean and what to do if something goes wrong.

explanation: Installation, starting, navigation, exiting.
hints: Think about the four tasks a client must do with the system.

stem: A project includes a routine that accepts a mark from 0 to 100. Write a test plan with six tests. Give the type of data, the input and the expected result for each. [6]

points.description: A standard test such as 65, accepted
A lower extreme test, 0, accepted
An upper extreme test, 100, accepted
An abnormal test just outside the range, such as 101 or -1, rejected with a message
An abnormal test of the wrong type, such as a letter, rejected
An empty input or another abnormal case, rejected, and every test has an expected result

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: 65 (standard) accepted; 0 (extreme) accepted; 100 (extreme) accepted; 101 (abnormal) rejected with an error message; the letter x (abnormal, wrong type) rejected; an empty entry (abnormal) rejected.

explanation: Standard, extreme and abnormal with expected results.
hints: Give a table with standard, extreme and abnormal data, each with an expected result.

stem: Describe how a learner should evaluate a finished project. [4]

points.description: Compare the system with each objective in the requirements specification
State which objectives were met and give the evidence from testing
State the limitations, honestly
Suggest improvements and opportunities for future development, and include the user's feedback

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Compare the system with each objective, saying which were met with the evidence from testing. State the limitations honestly, include the user's feedback and suggest improvements for the future.

explanation: Objectives, evidence, limitations, future.
hints: Compare the result with the objectives; mention limits and the future.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the result for the input 69.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the result for the input 49.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State the result for the input x7.
parts.explanation: x7 contains a letter, so isdigit() is false.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Classify the inputs 70, 100 and 101 as standard, extreme or abnormal data, and state the result of each.

points.description: 70 is extreme (a boundary between B and A) and the result is A
100 is extreme (upper limit) and the result is A
101 is abnormal (just outside the range) and the result is Invalid

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: 70 is a boundary value and gives A; 100 is the upper limit and gives A; 101 is abnormal and gives Invalid.

explanation: 69 gives B, 101 and x7 are invalid, and 49 gives U.
hints: Check the conditions in the order of the program.
Marks of 70 or more get an A; 50 to 69 a B.

stem: Nyasha is writing a stock-control program for a school tuck shop. One of her objectives is: "The system should be good."

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Explain why this objective is weak.

points.description: It is vague: the word good has no measure
It cannot be tested, so there is no way to show in the evaluation whether it was met

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It is vague because good cannot be measured, so it cannot be tested and the evaluation cannot show whether it was met.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Rewrite the objective as two specific, measurable objectives.

points.description: For example: the shop assistant can record a sale in under ten seconds
For example: the system warns the assistant when the stock of an item falls below a set level

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The shop assistant can record a sale in under ten seconds, and the system warns the assistant when the stock of an item falls below a set level.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe the evidence she should include to show that the first of the two new objectives has been met.

points.description: A timed trial with the assistant recording several sales, with the times written down
A screen shot or sample run, and the assistant's comment

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A timed trial with the assistant recording several sales, with the times written down, plus a screen shot or sample run and the assistant's comment.

explanation: Each objective needs a test and evidence; weak objectives cannot be tested.
hints: An objective should be specific and measurable.

stem: Tendai is in Form 5 in Hwange and has chosen to write a library system for his school as his project.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Give two reasons why this is a suitable choice of problem.

points.description: There is a real client (the librarian) who can answer questions and give feedback
It needs enough programming to show depth, such as files or a database, validation and reports

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There is a real client, the librarian, who can answer questions and give feedback, and it needs enough programming such as files or a database, validation and reports.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State two items of evidence he should put in the appendices.

points.description: Completed questionnaires or interview questions with the answers
Sample documents, such as the library's current loan cards or forms

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Completed questionnaires or interview answers, and sample documents such as the library's loan cards.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe two things that would make his code easy to read and maintain.

points.description: Meaningful names, comments, indentation and blank lines
Separate procedures and functions for each task, with local variables where possible

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Meaningful names, comments, indentation and blank lines, and separate procedures and functions for each task with local variables where possible.

explanation: A good project begins with real investigation and ends with an honest evaluation.
hints: Each part of the report has to show a different skill.
